answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

DATA SCOPE
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20; 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, covering 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL catalogue, the calibrated estimate):
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                       0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                       0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                       0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at/above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

INTERPRETATION
- The CALIBRATED estimate is the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue-based Shapiro et al. (2021) Eq. 5 result: even at the lowest b scenario (0.65), P(Mw>=5.5) is only ~0.0147/yr (~0.065% over the observed volume), i.e. a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is very unlikely under the calibrated model.
- The DAS-based number (P(Mw>=5.5) = 0.0784/yr at b = 0.9849) is an UPPER BOUND only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every detection is counted as an event at/above Mc, so it systematically over-counts and should not be used as a calibrated probability.
- Context: the run window shows net fluid extraction (net -4.048e+04 m3), and only 5 small catalogue events (ML -0.48 to 0.07) were recorded, while the DAS array flagged 57 anomalous records / 62 detections — consistent with the upper-bound DAS count over-counting relative to the calibrated catalogue.
